requirements.requirement: Configure a backend on node1 TCP port 8091 that returns `backend-ready`.
requirements.summary: Direct requests before and after restart received HTTP 200 with the exact body `backend-ready`; port 8091 was listening and its service recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Publish the backend through a reverse proxy on TCP port 8090.
requirements.summary: Requests to port 8090 returned HTTP 200 and `backend-ready`, with both backend and reverse-proxy headers demonstrating proxy traversal. The listener and firewall exposure persisted across reboot.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity, and recovered its system, services, listeners, firewall configuration, and responses. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot change and recovered listeners.
limitations: Publication was tested from node1 using its assigned IP rather than from a separate external client; listening and firewall observations provide supporting network-exposure evidence.
Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency was not independently assessed; the timeline shows no package installation or removal.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles in implementing, exposing, persisting, verifying, or restart-testing the services. The only unnecessary retained state was bounded staging residue: `/tmp/antrieb-http-stack.py` and its bytecode from cmd-8dc621bd518643b6, plus three temporary unit/template files from cmd-16e17504dc5349c8. All five remained after reboot and none was reverted. No failed services or other damage was observed.
